ai.title: Add DELETE token for file removal in CLI
ai.summary: Agent can delete files via [DELETE] token in file block body. applyChanges detects token, calls fs.unlinkSync. CLI logs Deleted instead of Created/Updated. Covers backend system-prompt, manicode project-files, cli.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the coding assistant to make changes, it can now remove files from your project outright instead of only creating or editing them. You'd see a line that says "Deleted" next to a file path in the terminal output when a file goes away. This is live today for anyone using the command-line tool.

ai.title: Add web scraping to knowledge files
ai.summary: System prompt now instructs agent to save helpful URLs in knowledge files. New `web-scraper.ts` in `manicode` uses `axios` and `cheerio` to fetch page content. `getProjectFileContext` in `project-files.ts` awaits scraping and appends content to knowledge files before sending context. This automates the ingestion of external documentation.

eli5.text: When you save a helpful webpage link (like API docs) into your project notes, the assistant now automatically reads that webpage's content and pastes it right into your notes too. So instead of just storing the link, you'll see the actual text from the page appear in your project files, making it easier to reference later without visiting the URL yourself. This works behind the scenes whenever the assistant checks your project files.

ai.title: Add many-updates diff generation test case
ai.summary: New mock fixture `many-updates` added to backend tests to exercise `generateDiffs` on a complex `ChatClient` file. The fixture provides `old.ts` and `new.ts` versions with distinct tool handler implementations and subscription logic. A corresponding test case in `prompts.test.ts` runs the diff generation against this fixture, ensuring the model correctly handles multiple structural changes in a single file update.

eli5.text: The team added a new test case that checks whether the assistant can correctly identify and handle a file that has been changed in many different ways all at once. This helps make sure the diff-generation feature stays reliable as the code evolves. You wouldn't notice anything directly, but it makes the system more robust behind the scenes.

ai.title: Remove message history from diffs prompt
ai.summary: Removed message history injection from the diffs generation prompt in backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts. The <message_history> block is stripped, leaving only the old file content and prompt instructions for diff calculation.

eli5.text: When you ask the system to figure out what changed between two versions of your file, it used to also read through the entire back-and-forth chat history that led up to the change. The system now skips that conversation history and only looks at the old version of the file itself when calculating the diff. This makes the diff calculation leaner and less likely to be influenced by past discussion; you'd notice if you reviewed the prompts the engine works from, which no longer include a message-history section.

ai.title: Add scrapewebpage tool with handler registry refactor
ai.summary: New `scrape_web_page` tool added to backend via `getTools` in `backend/src/tools.ts`, accepting a `url` string. `manicode/src/chat-client.ts` refactored to use a dynamic `toolHandlers` registry from new `manicode/src/tool-handlers.ts` instead of hardcoded `read_files` logic, enabling async execution. `handleScrapeWebPage` wraps output in `<web_scraped_content>` tags or returns `<web_scraping_error>` on failure. `backend/knowledge.md` updated with Web Scraping section.

eli5.text: The AI assistant can now fetch and read content from any web page you point it to, similar to how it already opens files in your project. Instead of only reading local files, you can give it a link to online documentation, APIs, or articles, and it will pull in the text so you can ask questions about it. Behind the scenes, the system was reworked to handle different tools through a shared registry, so adding capabilities like web scraping fits into the same flow as reading files. This is already live today, so if you ask the assistant to look at a URL, it can do it on the spot.

ai.title: Send error message as response-chunk in WebSocket
ai.summary: WebSocket handler wraps mainPrompt in try/catch. Extracts e.message, sends via response-chunk, then response-complete after 100ms. CLI suppresses 'Complete!' log if changesSuceeded is empty. Covers backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts and manicode/src/cli.ts.

eli5.text: When something goes wrong while the assistant is working through your request, you now see the specific error message appear live in your chat instead of the connection just stopping or showing nothing. The assistant catches the error, sends that message as a visible response, and then properly finishes the response after a brief pause. Additionally, the final 'Complete!' confirmation in the terminal tool now only appears when there were actual changes made, so you won't see it after a run that did nothing. Together, these changes mean failed attempts are more transparent to you, and successful tool output is cleaner.

ai.title: Remove auto-scrape from knowledge files
ai.summary: Removed automatic web scraping of URLs found in `knowledge.md` files during project context loading. `getProjectFileContext` now calls `getExistingFiles` instead of `getExistingFilesWithScrapedContent`, and the latter's scraping logic was deleted. The system prompt was updated to explicitly instruct the agent to use the `web_scrape` tool for URLs found in knowledge files or provided by the user, rather than relying on pre-loaded scraped content.

eli5.text: When you open a project that has a knowledge file listing web links, the assistant no longer automatically visits and downloads those pages for you. Instead, you now have to ask it to fetch any link yourself, using the new web scrape tool, right after it shows you the list of links. The assistant can still save useful links for you to read later, but it will just keep the link text, not the page contents.

ai.title: Restore automatic URL scraping for knowledge files
ai.summary: Re-enabled automatic scraping of URLs found in `knowledge.md` files. `getExistingFilesWithScrapedContent` now parses URLs and appends scraped web content within `<web_scraped_content>` tags. System prompt updated to reflect this behavior. Affects `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`, `manicode/src/index.ts`, and `manicode/src/project-files.ts`.

eli5.text: When you save a web link in your knowledge file for a project, the system now automatically fetches and includes the actual page content from that link right alongside the saved URL. This means links you've stored are no longer just addresses, the full text of the linked page is pulled in and added behind the scenes so you have the content available without visiting the link yourself. If you open a project that has saved knowledge files with URLs, you'll see the fetched web content appended in a dedicated section, as if it were always part of the file. This is live and active for all projects using knowledge files.

The assistant can now answer questions about uncertain future events by looking up live prediction markets. When you ask about something like an upcoming election, it searches a site called Manifold for yes-or-no betting markets on that topic and shows you each market's current probability as a forecast. Each result includes the market question, its probability, and a link to the full market. This works today as part of the assistant's internal tool set.

ai.title: Search Manifold Markets tool adds prediction market forecasts
ai.summary: Agent gains `search_manifold_markets` for future-event questions like presidential elections, returning Yes/No markets with probabilities to interpret as forecasts. It is defined in `backend/src/tools.ts` with `query` and `limit` inputs, handled in `manicode/src/tool-handlers.ts` by `handleSearchManifoldMarkets`, and implemented in new `manicode/src/manifold-api.ts`. The implementation queries `https://api.manifold.markets/v0/search-markets` with `contractType: BINARY`, defaults `limit` to 5, and returns `id`, `question`, `probability`, `url` as JSON, wrapping failures in `<manifold_search_error>`.

ai.title: CLI conditional file changes message
ai.summary: Updated `onStreamEnd` callback in `manicode/src/cli.ts` to accept the full response string. The 'Generating file changes' log now only prints if the response contains the `</file>` tag. This prevents misleading status updates when no file changes are generated.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something and it isn't going to change any files, the tool no longer prints a misleading 'Generating file changes' message that would make you sit and wait for something that won't happen. The message now only appears if the assistant's response actually contains file changes, so you won't be shown a fake status update when there's nothing to generate. This only affects people using the command-line version of the tool.
